taskfit.task: Real-estate speculative construction / absorption risk (Gurgaon, Jaipur, Dubai, Mumbai, London)
taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - 10 m pixels resolve construction footprints and annual angle-change flags new build 2017-2024; cannot see occupancy or absorption, which needs night-lights or transaction data; all five cities covered free in GEE
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - 10 m and CC0 are attractive but India, Dubai and Mexico have only the 2024 layer; London has 2017-2025; multi-year series needed for construction phasing is missing outside Europe/US
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 0 - 2.56 km cells (per Source Cooperative) average whole neighbourhoods and only June 2024 and June 2025 are published; cannot isolate projects
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 1 - 320 m chips can retrieve construction-like neighbourhoods for 2024 vs 2025 but two annual snapshots do not give a phasing series and chips mix several projects
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 0 - 2-4 km patches and a single snapshot; no temporal axis
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - OlmoEarth or Galileo on monthly Sentinel-1/2 give the quarterly cadence absorption analysis wants, but need a GPU pipeline per city and still cannot observe occupancy
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth annual change (dot product between years) to flag and date new construction, fused with VIIRS night-lights and OSM for absorption; escalate to OlmoEarth monthly embeddings only for the Gurgaon/Dubai pilots where quarterly phasing matters. Validate with buffered spatial CV and a stats-pooled parcel aggregate.

taskfit.task: Collateral change detection for mortgage lenders (property level)
taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - 10 m pixel is at the edge of single-property scale; angle between annual vectors is the documented change recipe; good as a screening layer, not as evidence
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - same resolution and better licence (CC0) but multi-year coverage only in US/Europe; outside those regions no prior-year layer exists
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 0 - 2.56 km chips cannot localise a property
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 0 - 320 m chips cover dozens of parcels; patch embedding dilutes a single-property change
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - TerraMind or Prithvi can be run on each new Sentinel-2 or HLS acquisition for event-driven checks; 10-30 m still marginal for a house; VHR imagery would need a different model
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth annual angle-change as a portfolio-wide screen (free, global, 2017-2024), with flagged parcels routed to VHR imagery or site inspection; in US/Europe use TESSERA v1.1 as a second opinion. Report precision at the lender's review-capacity threshold, not balanced accuracy.

taskfit.task: Commodity producer-region condition monitoring (cocoa, coffee, soy, wheat, sugar, palm, cotton) for price forecasting
taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 1 - excellent for extent and tree-crop mapping (Descals oil palm, crop tasks) but annual composite cannot track in-season condition that drives prices; use for acreage baseline only
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - same cadence limit; West Africa, Brazil, India have 2024 only
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 1 - monthly aggregated cadence is the right one and 2.56 km cells match district-level reporting, but only June 2024 and June 2025 are published on Source Cooperative; if LGND releases the full monthly archive this becomes a 3
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 1 - annual snapshots 2024 and 2025 only; useful for locating plantation and field clusters, not condition
taskfit.copernicus_embed: 0 - 2021 only, though 25 km cells would otherwise suit country-level signals
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 3 - Galileo and OlmoEarth ingest monthly Sentinel-1/2 time series and Presto-style pixel time series; TerraMind single-date; the only route to weekly/monthly condition embeddings over any producer region, at GPU cost
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: On-demand Galileo or OlmoEarth monthly embeddings over producer districts, with AlphaEarth used once to delineate the crop mask; benchmark against plain NDVI/ERA5 features and a persistence forecast before claiming uplift, since no published evaluation shows embeddings beat indices for in-season condition.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 3 - 10 m pixels suit 0.5-5 ha plantation blocks; AEF suite shows tree-genus (39-class) and oil-palm discrimination; India covered 2017-2024 so plantation age cohorts can be inferred; kNN with a few hundred field points is the documented protocol
taskfit.tessera_v11: 2 - 10 m, 128-d, CC0 and the Barlow Twins time-series encoder is well suited to phenology, but Gujarat has only the 2024 layer unless requested through GeoTessera; request 2019-2025 before the sprint
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 0 - 2.56 km cells swamp plantations in farmland
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - 320 m chips cover large contiguous blocks and the Earth Index 'find more like this' workflow is exactly how a plantation census is prospected; small or fragmented blocks will be missed
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - TerraMind or Galileo fine-tuned on Sentinel-2 time series would likely beat frozen embeddings, but the JK Paper project does not justify GPU pipeline cost when AlphaEarth kNN is free
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth kNN/linear probe at 10 m with field labels from the JK Paper live project, spatially blocked CV across talukas; use Earth Index for prospecting new blocks outside the labelled area; request TESSERA Gujarat 2019-2025 as a CC0 fallback.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - Ethiopia crops and Africa crop mask are in the AEF suite so coverage quality is demonstrated; pooled to DHS-cluster scale it is a strong covariate, but Rahman (2026) finds AEF encodes night-lights at only R2 0.58 and population density 0.56, so it is a complement to VIIRS, not a substitute
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - Kenya and Ethiopia have 2024 only; DHS waves 2014-2022 cannot be matched
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 2 - 2.56 km cells approximate the 2-5 km DHS cluster displacement radius; licence fine; but two months only and no history
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - 320 m chips pooled to clusters; two years; good for settlement-type retrieval
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 2 - patch scale matches cluster scale and SSL4EO-S1 adds radar for built-up detection; single snapshot and CC-BY-SA copyleft limit reuse in reports
taskfit.copernicus_embed: 1 - 25 km cells carry climate and regional context only; 2021 only
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - OlmoEarth monthly could track electrification dynamics but survey cadence does not require it
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth pooled with stats pooling to DHS clusters, fused with VIIRS night-lights, evaluated against SustainBench-style asset-wealth R2 with country-held-out splits; Major TOM SSL4EO-S1 as a radar cross-check if licence allows. Expect embeddings to add most where night-lights saturate or are dark.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - annual 2017-2024 matches annual budget data; pooled to gminas (about 100 km2) gives a long panel; CC-BY-4.0
taskfit.tessera_v11: 3 - Europe has full 2017-2025 coverage at 10 m, CC0 licence suits publication, 128-d gives more room for linear probes; the best-matched product for this task
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 2 - patch scale is right for gminas but only June 2024 and 2025
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - 320 m chips pool well to gminas; 2024-2025 only
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 2 - patch scale right; single snapshot; copyleft
taskfit.copernicus_embed: 1 - 25 km cells are larger than most gminas; 2021 only
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 1 - no cadence or resolution need that justifies GPU cost
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: TESSERA v1.1 pooled to gminas for a 2017-2025 panel (CC0, full European coverage), cross-checked with AlphaEarth 2017-2024; use the GUS fiscal series as target and report R2 under voivodeship-held-out CV so the result is defensible to a Polish audience.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - annual 10 m pixels pooled to counties capture canopy and built structure; 2017-2024 panel
taskfit.tessera_v11: 3 - US fully covered 2017-2025, CC0, 128-d; matches INFORMS DMDA outage panel years
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 2 - 2.56 km cells pool well to counties; two months only
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - 320 m chips pool to counties; two years
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 2 - patch scale fine; single snapshot; copyleft
taskfit.copernicus_embed: 1 - 25 km cells coarser than many eastern counties; 2021 only
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 1 - exposure is slow-changing; no need for on-demand cadence
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: TESSERA v1.1 county aggregates (stats pooling) for exposure covariates alongside AlphaEarth as a robustness check; the embedding should be judged by uplift in outage-count R2 over the existing weather and infrastructure covariates, not by land-cover accuracy.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - 10 m pixels pooled to blocks or 250 m hexes capture urban form (So2Sat-type LCZ discrimination shown in host benchmarks); Mexico covered 2017-2024
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - 320 m chips are close to neighbourhood scale and retrieval of similar urban fabric is a natural feature; two years
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 1 - 2-4 km patches too coarse for blocks
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 1 - urban form changes slowly; on-demand not needed unless VHR is used
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth with stats pooling to 250 m H3 cells as the urban-form covariate, Earth Index 320 m for 'similar neighbourhood' retrieval; validate against INEGI DENUE openings/closures with buffered spatial CV, and compare to a LCZ or OSM-density baseline.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - unit-norm vectors make cosine search trivial and GEE angle queries work, but it is a pixel product with no published ANN index; patch-level search needs pooling and an external vector store
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - same pixel limitation plus partial coverage; no index
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 2 - designed for similarity search in GeoParquet, 1024-d, global; 2.56 km cells are coarse for anything smaller than a landscape unit
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 3 - built for retrieval: 320 m chips, global, two years, Earth Index UI and GeoParquet with STAC metadata; the only product with retrieval as its primary use
taskfit.majortom_dinov2_siglip_ssl4eo: 2 - designed for search, four encoders, global; coarse 2-4 km patches and CC-BY-SA copyleft
taskfit.copernicus_embed: 1 - 25 km cells retrieve climate analogues only
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 1 - you must generate and index your own embeddings; no product
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: Earth Index for facility-to-landscape retrieval; pooled AlphaEarth in a FAISS index when 10 m detail matters. Evaluate with precision@k against analyst-judged relevance on at least 50 queries, since no product publishes a relevance metric.

taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 3 - the only product with a consistent annual series (2017-2024) and documented dot-product change guidance; free in GEE; AEF suite reports 78-79 percent balanced accuracy on supervised LCMAP change
taskfit.tessera_v11: 2 - multi-year only in US and Europe; elsewhere a single 2024 layer so no change possible yet
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 1 - June 2024 vs June 2025 only; patch scale
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 1 - 2024 vs 2025 only, and the two years use different encoders (SoftCon vs SSL4EO) so vectors are not comparable across years
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - can produce any pair of dates, including monthly, but cost scales with area and embedding drift across Sentinel-2 processing baselines must be controlled
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth annual angle change with a no-change control set to calibrate the threshold; in US/Europe TESSERA v1.1 as a second series. Note that Earth Index 2024 and 2025 are not comparable across years because the encoder changed.

taskfit.task: Spatial transfer (train in one city, apply in another)
taskfit.alphaearth_v1: 2 - globally consistent encoder and training on 1.1 percent of land argue for transfer, but the only published test (EuroSAT longitude split) shows an 8.8 pp drop with mean pooling, cut to 3.8 pp with stats pooling; city-to-city transfer is untested
taskfit.tessera_v11: 1 - transfer requires both cities to have the same years; outside US/Europe only 2024 is shared
taskfit.clay_lgnd_v15: 1 - consistent global model but coarse patches; untested
taskfit.earthindex_v7: 2 - consistent global snapshot per year; retrieval-style transfer is its design use; untested quantitatively
taskfit.ondemand_prithvi_terramind_galileo_olmoe: 2 - same weights everywhere, but input preprocessing and Sentinel-2 baseline differences between cities introduce shift the frozen products have already absorbed
taskfit.recommended_product_and_why: AlphaEarth with stats or covariance pooling, trained in city A and evaluated in city B with a buffered spatial split and a hand-crafted covariate baseline; publish the geographic generalisation gap as the headline number. This is the experiment the literature lacks and would be a credible sprint contribution.

questions.q: Does this product actually cover my area and years?
questions.explain: Share of grid cells in the area with a valid vector, per year.

questions.q: How much of the imagery signal does the vector keep?
questions.explain: Blocked R2 of a ridge probe from the embedding to Sentinel-2 vegetation (NDVI), built-up (NDBI) and brightness indices.

questions.q: Is the same place represented the same way next year if nothing changed?
questions.explain: Median cosine similarity of the same cell across consecutive years, on cells with under 2 pp of GHSL built-up change.

questions.q: Does 'near' in embedding space mean 'near' on the ground?
questions.explain: Mean cosine similarity by hex-ring distance; the drop from ring 1 to ring 8 shows how much geography the vectors encode.

questions.q: Find more places like this one: how precise is it?
questions.explain: precision@10 of cosine nearest neighbours sharing the WorldCover 2021 majority class, against the chance level.

questions.q: Can it predict what the ground looks like now (built-up, crops, trees)?
questions.explain: Blocked R2 of a ridge probe predicting GHSL built-up fraction 2020 and WorldCover 2021 class fractions; spatial blocks, block bootstrap interval.

questions.q: Does the year-on-year movement of the vector match real change?
questions.explain: Spearman correlation and AUC of embedding displacement against GHSL and WorldCover built-up change.

questions.q: Can today's vector flag where building will happen next?
questions.explain: Blocked R2 and AUC predicting GHSL built-up change 2020-2025 from the 2020 embedding (the 2025 GHSL epoch is modelled).

questions.q: Does a model trained in one city hold in another?
questions.explain: Out-of-region R2 and the transfer gap (in-region blocked R2 minus out-of-region R2).

questions.q: How much do random splits flatter this product?
questions.explain: Random-split R2 minus spatially blocked R2 on the same target: the matched-backtest leakage control.

dubai_emirate_osm.alphaearth_v1: AlphaEarth Foundations V1 on Dubai emirate (OSM administrative). Years evaluated: 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025; cells with a valid vector 0.80 of the area. Represent: the vectors keep n/a of the Sentinel-2 vegetation signal and n/a of the built-up signal (blocked R2); effective rank 2.2 dimensions; the same unchanged cell has a median cosine of 0.989 to itself a year later. Relate: Moran's I of the first component 0.98; similarity falls by 0.080 from one to eight hex rings; retrieval precision@10 0.97 (lift over chance 0.52). Reason: a ridge probe predicts the 2020 built-up fraction with blocked R2 0.82 (strong), cropland -0.09, tree cover 0.48; embedding displacement flags top-decile built-up change with AUC 0.73; the 2020 vector flags 2020-2025 growth with AUC 0.89. Transfer: random splits overstate the built-up R2 by 0.074; out-of-region R2 0.41 (transfer gap 14.97). Serve: estimated pull 42163 MB, about 28 minutes at 25 MB/s; no login required. Fit for use: yes for current-state mapping and retrieval; change screening worth testing further.
